1 خَالَ , aor. يَخُولُ, inf. n. خَوْلٌ, He became possessed of خَوَل [so I read, meaning slaves, or servants, and other dependents, in the place of خوال, an evident mistranscription, in the TA,] after having been alone. (TA.) ―
-b2- فُلَانٌ يَخُولُ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ Such a one pastures for his family: (S:) or يَخُولُ عَلَيْهِمْ signifies he milks and waters and pastures for them. (T, TA.) And خال عَلَيْهِمْ He ruled, or governed, them. (JK.) And خال مَالَهُ, (K, * TA,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. خَوْلٌ and خِيَالٌ, (K,) He pastured his cattle, or camels &c., and managed them, or tended them, and sustained them, (K, * TA,) well: (K:) or خُلْتُ المَالَ, aor. أَخُولُ, I managed the cattle, &c., well: (S:) and خال عَلَى المَالِ, aor. يَخُولُ, he pastured the cattle, &c., and managed them well; as also خال, aor. يَخِيلُ. (TA in art. خيل.) ＝
-A2- خال, aor. يَخُولُ and يَخَالُ or يَخِيلُ, see اختال (with which it is syn.) in art. خيل.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
